reference.label: OTN cross-connect
reference.definition: A network element whose switching fabric maps ODUs between line and client-facing interfaces.
reference.example: The cross-connect switches an ODU from a 400-Gbit/s line card to client port 7.

reference.label: client port
reference.definition: A customer-facing interface that maps a client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100-Gbit/s client port maps an Ethernet service into an ODU.

reference.label: optical amplifier
reference.definition: A line-system unit that raises the optical power of a multiplexed wavelength signal.
reference.example: An EDFA amplifies all 40 wavelengths on an optical span.

reference.label: booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier located at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A booster raises launch power before the wavelength band enters the first fibre span.

reference.label: inline amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at an intermediate site that forwards wavelengths without terminating them.
reference.example: An inline amplifier restores power after an 80-km span.

reference.label: preamplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A preamplifier boosts arriving channels before they enter the receiving ROADM.

reference.label: intermediate amplifier site
reference.definition: An intermediate line site housing an inline amplifier and terminating and regenerating supervision.
reference.example: The shelter contains an inline amplifier and originates supervision for the next span.

reference.label: wavelength router
reference.definition: A photonic switching resource that independently steers optical channels between line directions.
reference.example: The router sends wavelength λ1 south and λ2 east from the same west input.

reference.label: coherent line interface
reference.definition: An interface that originates or terminates a coherent optical channel.
reference.example: A coherent line interface terminates a 400-Gbit/s wavelength at each end of a lightpath.

reference.label: transponder
reference.definition: A line interface that maps one client service onto one optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder carries one 400-Gbit/s client over a dedicated wavelength.

reference.label: muxponder
reference.definition: A line interface that aggregates several lower-rate client signals onto one optical channel.
reference.example: A muxponder combines four 100-Gbit/s clients onto one 400-Gbit/s wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A coherent optical line module connected to an ODU switching fabric.
reference.example: An OTN line card receives an ODU from the switch fabric and transmits it on a wavelength.

reference.label: protection selector
reference.definition: A function that selects between working and protection ODU paths at the receiving endpoint.
reference.example: The destination client port selects the healthy protection path after the working path fails.

reference.label: fibre cut
reference.definition: A complete physical break in a fibre span that prevents optical signals from passing.
reference.example: Excavation severs the cable and removes both traffic light and supervision downstream.

reference.label: span loss increase
reference.definition: An increase in fibre-path attenuation caused by bending, splicing, stress, or similar damage.
reference.example: A cable bend adds 12 dB of span loss and sharply reduces received power.

reference.label: disconnected optical jumper
reference.definition: A connector or patch cord disconnected at a port or patch panel, opening the optical path.
reference.example: A technician removes the section-head patch cord and the far end loses all light.

reference.label: dirty optical connector
reference.definition: Contamination on an optical connector that introduces loss, reflection, or signal penalty.
reference.example: Dust on a connector raises pre-FEC errors until the end-face is cleaned.

reference.label: amplifier outage
reference.definition: Failure of an amplifier or its pump that leaves the amplifier with no usable optical output.
reference.example: Loss of pump power makes every wavelength disappear from the amplifier output.

reference.label: amplifier gain drop
reference.definition: An amplifier impairment in which actual gain falls below its configured value.
reference.example: An amplifier set for 20 dB provides only 16 dB of gain.

reference.label: amplifier noise increase
reference.definition: An increase in amplifier-added noise that lowers channel OSNR, possibly without changing power.
reference.example: A faulty amplifier preserves output level but lowers every channel's OSNR.

reference.label: amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: Non-flat amplifier gain that affects one part of the optical band more than another.
reference.example: Channels at the long-wavelength band edge leave 3 dB weaker than centre channels.

reference.label: pump wear
reference.definition: Gradual amplifier-pump ageing that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain.
reference.example: Normalized pump current rises from 100% to 121% over two years.

reference.label: transmit laser failure
reference.definition: Failure of a line interface's transmit laser or drive circuitry that stops optical emission.
reference.example: A laser-driver failure makes the far-end receiver lose the wavelength.

reference.label: line card failure
reference.definition: Failure of a complete line-interface card, removing traffic and valid card telemetry.
reference.example: A failed line card loses both traffic directions and stops reporting measurements.

reference.label: receiver degradation
reference.definition: A receiver-local defect that adds decoding penalty without impairing the transmitted path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver reports errors while peer channels and the optical route remain healthy.

reference.label: transmit laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive laser ageing evidenced by increasing bias current and possible eventual failure.
reference.example: Laser bias rises to 125% of its initial value before the transmitter becomes dark.

reference.label: channel margin erosion
reference.definition: A gradual decline in an optical channel's remaining performance margin.
reference.example: Estimated channel margin falls from 5 dB to 2 dB over several months.

reference.label: channel attenuation error
reference.definition: Incorrect per-channel attenuation at a wavelength-selective switch or router.
reference.example: Excess attenuation leaves λ8 four decibels below its required router output level.

reference.label: WSS passband shift
reference.definition: Frequency misalignment of a WSS passband that clips or narrows one optical channel.
reference.example: A filter offset clips λ12 even though its measured total power remains normal.

reference.label: WSS port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a WSS directional port that blocks all channels entering through that port.
reference.example: A failed west input blocks west-arriving channels while north-input traffic continues.

reference.label: DGD increase
reference.definition: An increase in differential group delay that reduces coherent-receiver tolerance.
reference.example: DGD rises from 8 ps to 35 ps and causes channel degradation.

reference.label: state-of-polarisation transient
reference.definition: A rapid temporary change in optical state of polarisation that may outrun receiver tracking.
reference.example: Movement of an aerial cable causes polarization to rotate faster than the receiver can follow.

reference.label: mechanical fibre disturbance
reference.definition: A brief physical disturbance of fibre or a patch panel that causes a loss excursion.
reference.example: Movement of a patch panel causes a momentary two-decibel power dip.

reference.label: channel-loading transient
reference.definition: A brief multiplex power disturbance produced when optical channels are added or removed.
reference.example: Adding eight channels causes a short power excursion across the optical section.

reference.label: protection-switch interruption
reference.definition: A brief service interruption produced while protection changes the selected path.
reference.example: The client experiences a 50-ms interruption while traffic switches to protection.

reference.label: OTN switching-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN switch fabric that interrupts every ODU traversing that fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric card simultaneously drops all 40 ODUs through the node.

reference.label: ODU cross-connect misconfiguration
reference.definition: An incorrect ODU mapping that delivers one connection to the wrong endpoint.
reference.example: Customer A's ODU is configured to customer B's client port.

reference.label: client-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a customer-facing port, its optic, or its local interface hardware.
reference.example: A failed 100-Gbit/s client optic interrupts the attached customer service.

reference.label: instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring defect in which an instrument reports an incorrect value.
reference.example: A power monitor reports −30 dBm while an external meter measures −10 dBm.

reference.label: stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitoring defect in which a previously valid value remains frozen and is no longer current.
reference.example: Receive power remains displayed at −12 dBm after the input fibre is removed.

reference.label: unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: A non-specific failure somewhere upstream on the signal path to the observing endpoint.
reference.example: A received AIS is attributed to an unspecified earlier failure on the path.

reference.label: unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: A non-specific failure in a server layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: An ODU alarm is attributed to an unspecified optical or OTU server failure.

reference.label: unspecified fault
reference.definition: A deliberately non-specific fault category used when no narrower cause is identified.
reference.example: A protection-state indication cites an unspecified fault because many failures can trigger switching.

reference.label: optical signal absent
reference.definition: No detectable optical signal, or power below the receiver's detection threshold.
reference.example: The line receiver measures no light after the upstream fibre is cut.

reference.label: optical power low
reference.definition: Optical signal power is below its expected or required level but is still detectable.
reference.example: The receiver sees −24 dBm where at least −18 dBm is required.

reference.label: optical supervisory channel lost
reference.definition: The optical supervisory channel is absent on one supervised fibre span.
reference.example: A span cut removes supervision between two adjacent amplifier sites.

reference.label: optical power excursion
reference.definition: A brief dip or swing in optical power lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Channel loading causes a two-second drop in aggregate output power.

reference.label: low OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio is reduced enough to threaten or impair decoding.
reference.example: OSNR falls to 10 dB and the coherent receiver begins counting errors.

reference.label: rapid polarisation change
reference.definition: State of polarisation changes faster than the coherent receiver can reliably track.
reference.example: Fast polarization rotation causes bursts of uncorrectable errors.

reference.label: high differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay exceeds the receiver's reliable operating tolerance.
reference.example: DGD reaches 40 ps on a receiver rated for 25 ps.

reference.label: optical filter penalty
reference.definition: Signal quality is reduced by spectral narrowing or misalignment while total power may remain normal.
reference.example: A shifted passband clips one spectral edge although channel power is still −2 dBm.

reference.label: receiver-local penalty
reference.definition: A degradation introduced by one receiver that does not propagate along the optical path.
reference.example: Only the destination receiver reports errors while an external analyzer shows a healthy signal.

reference.label: unit down
reference.definition: A unit has failed, carries no traffic, and supplies no valid operational telemetry.
reference.example: A failed line card stops traffic and ceases reporting power and temperature.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: Loss of OTU frame alignment at a line receiver, whether or not optical light remains present.
reference.example: The receiver has normal optical power but cannot maintain OTU framing.

reference.label: OTU degradation
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors exceed the degradation threshold while OTU framing remains aligned.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER rises above 1×10^-3 while the receiver remains frame-aligned.

reference.label: ODU AIS present
reference.definition: An ODU Alarm Indication Signal is travelling downstream on an affected ODU path.
reference.example: An upstream line failure causes the destination client port to receive ODU AIS.

reference.label: ODU misdelivery
reference.definition: An ODU is delivered to an endpoint other than its intended destination.
reference.example: A port expecting customer A's trace receives customer B's ODU.

reference.label: client service down
reference.definition: The client service is interrupted in the affected direction.
reference.example: Failure of a client optic interrupts the customer's Ethernet service.

reference.label: brief client interruption
reference.definition: A short client-visible service interruption, typically during protection switching.
reference.example: Traffic pauses for 50 ms while the selector moves to the protection path.

reference.label: pump ageing indication
reference.definition: Amplifier pump current is increasing over time to maintain the configured gain.
reference.example: Pump drive rises steadily from 100% to 115% while service remains healthy.

reference.label: laser ageing indication
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current is increasing over time as the laser ages.
reference.example: Laser bias climbs from 100% to 118% of its commissioning value.

reference.label: channel margin decline
reference.definition: An optical channel's estimated performance margin is decreasing gradually.
reference.example: The receiver reports a margin decline of 0.2 dB per month.

reference.label: dark amplifier output with live input
reference.definition: An amplifier has valid optical input but produces no detectable optical output.
reference.example: The amplifier input is −10 dBm but its output is dark.
synonyms: no light although light is entering

reference.label: amplifier gain deviation
reference.definition: Actual amplifier gain differs materially from its configured gain.
reference.example: An amplifier configured for 18 dB produces only 15.5 dB.

reference.label: pump-drive end-of-life threshold
reference.definition: Normalized amplifier pump drive exceeds 120% of its commissioning reference.
reference.example: Pump drive reaches 121%, crossing the end-of-life threshold.

reference.label: laser-bias ageing threshold
reference.definition: Normalized transmit-laser bias exceeds 120% of its commissioning reference.
reference.example: Laser bias reaches 123%, indicating advanced laser ageing.

reference.label: traffic on protection path
reference.definition: The protection selector is currently forwarding service over the protection ODU path.
reference.example: After the working path fails, the selector carries traffic over route B.

reference.label: protection path unavailable
reference.definition: The configured protection ODU path is defective and cannot provide redundancy.
reference.example: The protection route begins receiving AIS while traffic remains on the working route.

reference.label: remote defect reported
reference.definition: The far endpoint reports a defect in the signal transmitted by the local endpoint.
reference.example: The peer cannot decode the local signal and returns a backward defect indication.

reference.label: aggregate amplifier input power
reference.definition: Total optical power of all channels at an amplifier input.
reference.example: The amplifier reports −4 dBm total input power across 40 channels.
synonyms: aggregate optical power entering the module

reference.label: aggregate amplifier output power
reference.definition: Total optical power of all channels at an amplifier output.
reference.example: The amplifier reports +16 dBm aggregate output power.
synonyms: aggregate optical power leaving the module

reference.label: normalized pump current
reference.definition: Amplifier pump current expressed as a percentage of its initial or commissioning reference.
reference.example: A value of 115% means the pump is driven 15% harder than at commissioning.

reference.label: normalized laser bias
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its initial or commissioning reference.
reference.example: A laser-bias reading of 122% accompanies an ageing warning.

reference.label: per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for each channel at an optical channel monitor.
reference.example: The channel monitor reports λ1 at −2.1 dBm and λ2 at −5.4 dBm.

reference.label: per-channel OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio measured separately for each channel by a channel monitor.
reference.example: The ROADM channel monitor reports 18 dB OSNR for λ7.

reference.label: received optical power
reference.definition: Instantaneous optical power measured at a line receiver.
reference.example: The line receiver reports −12.5 dBm.

reference.label: received-power 15-minute statistic
reference.definition: Received optical power summarized in a 15-minute performance-monitoring bin.
reference.example: The latest 15-minute bin records a minimum receive power of −14.2 dBm.

reference.label: line errored seconds
reference.definition: Count of seconds in which the monitored line signal contains one or more errors.
reference.example: Errors during five distinct seconds add five line errored seconds.

reference.label: estimated OSNR
reference.definition: OSNR estimated by a coherent receiver's digital signal processor.
reference.example: The coherent receiver estimates an OSNR of 14.8 dB.

reference.label: pre-FEC bit error ratio
reference.definition: The received bit error ratio measured before forward-error correction.
reference.example: The receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 2×10^-4.

reference.label: differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay estimated for a received coherent optical channel.
reference.example: The receiver reports 18 ps of DGD.

reference.label: polarisation change rate
reference.definition: The measured rate of change of the received state of polarisation.
reference.example: A rise to 50 krad/s indicates rapid polarization movement.

reference.label: client errored seconds
reference.definition: Count of seconds in which the monitored client service contains one or more errors.
reference.example: Errors in 12 distinct seconds produce 12 client errored seconds.

reference.label: client unavailable seconds
reference.definition: Count of seconds during which the monitored client service is declared unavailable.
reference.example: A 90-second client outage adds 90 unavailable seconds.

reference.label: supervisory-link receive status
reference.definition: A Boolean status stating whether the incoming optical supervisory link is being received.
reference.example: The status changes to false after the supervisory channel is interrupted.

reference.label: alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A monitor that raises state alarms but does not expose a numeric measurement value.
reference.example: An OSC receiver raises loss of supervision without reporting received power.

reference.label: TRIB-FAIL
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating failure of the client service on a tributary port.
reference.example: A failed client optic drops service and raises TRIB-FAIL.

reference.label: AIS-IN
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that ODU AIS is being received at a tributary port.
reference.example: An upstream line failure inserts AIS and the destination port raises AIS-IN.

reference.label: REMOTE-AIS
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that the remote endpoint reports receiving ODU AIS.
reference.example: The peer reports AIS on the transmitted ODU, causing REMOTE-AIS locally.

reference.label: TRACE-MISMATCH
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that the arriving ODU identity does not match the expected identity.
reference.example: Customer B's trace arrives at customer A's port and raises TRACE-MISMATCH.

reference.label: ON-STANDBY
reference.definition: A vendor state indication that the protection selector is using the standby ODU route.
reference.example: The port raises ON-STANDBY after selecting route B.

reference.label: STANDBY-LOST
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating loss of the standby ODU route and its protection capability.
reference.example: AIS on the standby path causes STANDBY-LOST while working traffic remains active.

reference.label: TRIB-HW
reference.definition: A vendor alarm localizing a physical hardware fault to a tributary port.
reference.example: A failed interface ASIC on the client port raises TRIB-HW.

reference.label: FABRIC-HW
reference.definition: A vendor alarm localizing a physical fault to an OTN switching fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric card raises FABRIC-HW.

reference.label: IN-DARK
reference.definition: A vendor inline-amplifier alarm indicating absence of optical input light.
reference.example: A fibre cut before the inline amplifier raises IN-DARK.

reference.label: SEC-IN-DARK
reference.definition: A vendor preamplifier alarm indicating that an optical section arrives without light.
reference.example: A disconnected launch patch lead causes SEC-IN-DARK at the receiving end.

reference.label: SV-LOSS
reference.definition: A vendor amplifier alarm indicating loss of the incoming supervisory link.
reference.example: A span cut prevents receipt of supervision and raises SV-LOSS.

reference.label: OUT-DARK
reference.definition: A vendor amplifier alarm indicating no optical output despite valid optical input.
reference.example: An amplifier with −10 dBm input and zero output raises OUT-DARK.

reference.label: GAIN-DEV
reference.definition: A vendor amplifier alarm raised when actual gain differs from its setting by more than 2 dB.
reference.example: An amplifier set to 20 dB delivers 17 dB and raises GAIN-DEV.

reference.label: PUMP-EOL
reference.definition: A vendor end-of-life alarm raised when normalized pump drive exceeds 120%.
reference.example: Pump drive reaches 121% and the amplifier raises PUMP-EOL.

reference.label: RX-DARK
reference.definition: A vendor line-interface alarm indicating that the receiver detects no optical light.
reference.example: A remote laser failure causes the receiving terminal to raise RX-DARK.

reference.label: FRAME-LOSS
reference.definition: A vendor line-interface alarm indicating loss of OTU framing while optical light may remain present.
reference.example: Severe noise prevents frame synchronization and raises FRAME-LOSS.

reference.label: DEGRADE
reference.definition: A vendor line-interface alarm raised when pre-FEC errors exceed the degradation threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises BER above threshold and triggers DEGRADE.

reference.label: REMOTE-DEFECT
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that the far endpoint reports a defect in the locally transmitted signal.
reference.example: The peer returns a defect indication and the local terminal raises REMOTE-DEFECT.

reference.label: TX-HW
reference.definition: A vendor alarm localizing a hardware fault to the transmit laser or its circuitry.
reference.example: A laser-driver failure raises TX-HW.

reference.label: MOD-HW
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating failure of a wavelength-terminal module as a whole.
reference.example: A failed module controller stops telemetry and raises MOD-HW.

reference.label: TX-BIAS
reference.definition: A vendor ageing alarm raised when normalized transmit-laser bias exceeds 120%.
reference.example: Laser bias reaches 124% and the terminal raises TX-BIAS.

reference.label: all optical channels
reference.definition: Every optical channel in the affected multiplexed signal or component.
reference.example: An amplifier outage removes all 32 channels it carried.

reference.label: one optical channel
reference.definition: A single optical channel considered independently of neighboring channels.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband degrades λ12 while other channels remain healthy.

reference.label: subset of optical channels
reference.definition: Some but not all channels of a multiplexed optical signal.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens only the channels at one edge of the band.

reference.label: directional optical input
reference.definition: All channels entering a ROADM through one directional input port.
reference.example: A west-port failure blocks every channel arriving from the west.

reference.label: switching fabric
reference.definition: The internal matrix and control elements that switch ODUs within an OTN cross-connect.
reference.example: A failed fabric card affects the matrix carrying all ODUs through the node.

reference.label: all traversing ODUs
reference.definition: Every ODU cross-connected through the affected switching fabric.
reference.example: A fabric outage interrupts all 40 ODUs traversing the switch.

reference.label: one ODU
reference.definition: A single Optical Data Unit rather than the full set carried through a switch.
reference.example: A wrong mapping misroutes only customer A's ODU.

reference.label: one cross-connect connection
reference.definition: A single provisioned logical ODU mapping through a cross-connect.
reference.example: The mapping from line ODU2 to client port 7 is one connection.

reference.label: client service
reference.definition: The end-user traffic service carried through the network.
reference.example: A protection switch briefly interrupts the customer's Ethernet service.

reference.label: current unit
reference.definition: The specific equipment unit that raised an alarm or observed a condition.
reference.example: PUMP-EOL is raised by the current inline amplifier.

reference.label: current port
reference.definition: The specific client or line port that raised an alarm.
reference.example: TRIB-HW identifies a hardware fault in the current client port.

reference.label: immediately upstream fibre span
reference.definition: The fibre span directly preceding the observing unit in signal direction.
reference.example: A bend in the upstream span reduces the amplifier's input power.

reference.label: immediately upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The amplifier before the fibre span that directly precedes the observing unit.
reference.example: Failure of the upstream amplifier makes the next amplifier's input dark.

reference.label: optical-section input patch
reference.definition: The input connection or patch at the transmitting head of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: Disconnecting the section input patch removes light at the distant preamplifier.
synonyms: patch lead at the section head

reference.label: upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The channel or WSS input port at the immediately preceding ROADM on the signal path.
reference.example: The channel first becomes weak at the output of the upstream ROADM.

reference.label: upstream on the optical path
reference.definition: Any relevant fibre, amplifier, patch, or ROADM point before the observing unit.
reference.example: Noise introduced upstream remains visible at the receiving terminal.

reference.label: far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting toward the current receiver.
reference.example: Failure of the far-end transmitter causes the local receiver to lose light.

reference.label: far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the signal transmitted by the current unit.
reference.example: The far-end receiver reports a defect in the locally transmitted wavelength.

reference.label: path from far end
reference.definition: The complete incoming path from and including the far-end line interface to the current unit.
reference.example: An RX-DARK cause may lie anywhere on the path from the far-end transmitter.
synonyms: between here and the other end

reference.label: either client endpoint
reference.definition: Either client-facing endpoint of the same carried service.
reference.example: Failure of a client port at either endpoint can interrupt the service.

reference.label: ODU-path cross-connect
reference.definition: An OTN switch or cross-connect traversed by a service's ODU path.
reference.example: A fabric outage at an intermediate ODU switch interrupts the service.

reference.label: working ODU path
reference.definition: The preferred ODU path used under normal protected operation.
reference.example: Traffic uses the working path until a defect causes protection switching.

reference.label: protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU path reserved to protect the working path.
reference.example: The selector moves traffic to the protection path after the working path fails.

reference.label: active ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU path currently carrying the service, whether working or protection.
reference.example: After switching, the protection route becomes the active ODU path.

reference.label: downstream
reference.definition: After the referenced component in the direction of signal propagation.
reference.example: Amplifier-added noise is observed at downstream receivers.

reference.label: baseline monitoring
reference.definition: Standard monitoring available on every unit, including alarms and basic performance counters.
reference.example: Baseline monitoring reports alarms and 15-minute errored-second counts.

reference.label: optical-power monitoring
reference.definition: An optional capability exposing detailed input, output, and received optical-power values.
reference.example: Enabling power monitoring adds aggregate amplifier input and output readings.

reference.label: optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: A capability exposing per-channel power and OSNR at wavelength-routing points.
reference.example: The channel monitor reports individual power and OSNR for every ROADM channel.

reference.label: advanced coherent telemetry
reference.definition: Advanced telemetry exposing coherent-DSP metrics and normalized equipment-health currents.
reference.example: Advanced telemetry provides estimated OSNR, DGD, pump current, and laser bias.

reference.label: hard outage
reference.definition: An abrupt event that makes the affected traffic or resource unavailable.
reference.example: A fibre cut causes an immediate hard outage.

reference.label: soft degradation
reference.definition: An impairment in which traffic remains present but its quality or margin is reduced.
reference.example: Increased amplifier noise lowers OSNR without immediately dropping traffic.

reference.label: incipient fault
reference.definition: A developing trend that precedes failure while traffic is not yet materially affected.
reference.example: Rising pump current warns of ageing before gain is lost.

reference.label: slow evolution
reference.definition: A condition that changes gradually over an extended period rather than abruptly.
reference.example: Laser bias rises slowly over several months.

reference.label: transient event
reference.definition: A brief event lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: A mechanical disturbance causes a one-second power dip.

reference.label: provisioning outage
reference.definition: Service unavailability caused by incorrect configuration, usually following provisioning work.
reference.example: A newly changed ODU mapping sends the service to the wrong client port.

reference.label: critical severity
reference.definition: The highest operational severity, requiring prompt response to actual or imminent service loss.
reference.example: Loss of light on an in-service wavelength is classified as critical.

reference.label: major severity
reference.definition: A significant condition requiring attention but below the highest urgency tier.
reference.example: Loss of the protection path while working traffic remains active is major.

reference.label: minor severity
reference.definition: A low-priority warning or maintenance condition with little or no current service effect.
reference.example: An early pump-ageing warning is classified as minor.

reference.label: non-alarmed information
reference.definition: A reported operational condition that is informational rather than an alarm requiring repair.
reference.example: Successful use of the protection path is reported as non-alarmed information.

reference.label: dual-path ODU protection
reference.definition: Protection behavior in which a receiving selector chooses between working and protection ODU paths.
reference.example: When the working path receives AIS, the selector moves the service to the clean protection path.

reference.label: per-channel wavelength routing
reference.definition: Routing behavior in which every optical channel is switched independently of other channels.
reference.example: A ROADM sends λ1 north and λ2 east even though both arrived from the west.

reference.label: transparent condition forwarding
reference.definition: Behavior that forwards an arriving signal or condition without logically terminating or changing it.
reference.example: The cross-connect transparently passes received ODU AIS to the provisioned egress.

reference.label: default condition handling
reference.definition: The fallback behavior applied when no more specific condition-handling rule matches.
reference.example: An unrecognized incoming impairment is processed by the default rule.

reference.label: fixed-gain amplification
reference.definition: Amplifier behavior that retains commissioned gain instead of compensating for later input-power changes.
reference.example: A 4-dB input drop produces a 4-dB output drop because gain remains fixed.

reference.label: span-by-span supervision regeneration
reference.definition: Behavior in which each amplifier site terminates the incoming supervisory link and originates a new one.
reference.example: Loss of supervision between sites 2 and 3 does not spread to the next span.

reference.label: channel power equalization
reference.definition: ROADM behavior that restores a channel's output power when the required correction is within range.
reference.example: A channel arriving 7 dB low is restored to its configured launch level.

reference.label: power restoration without OSNR restoration
reference.definition: Behavior in which level equalization restores channel power but cannot remove prior OSNR loss.
reference.example: The ROADM restores output power, but the channel remains 3 dB worse in OSNR.

reference.label: OTU-failure consequent action
reference.definition: Terminal behavior after OTU frame loss that inserts downstream ODU AIS and returns a defect indication.
reference.example: After losing OTU framing, the terminal sends ODU AIS downstream and reports the defect backward.
